Excellent

The new Things is clearly a powerful and sleek beast . I haven't though seen many reviews of Things iOS that mention downsides . I do wonder how anyone can assess a new app thoroughly enough to confidently award 5 stars, within days of its release . To perhaps redress the balance (or is it an 'outpouring of negativity'), here are my rough jottings of aspects of Things 3 that I find a turn off:
Loss of functionality from Things 2 as listed in the Things Support article e.g. Projects list gone, can no longer set an advance warning of a deadline, can no longer filter by 'no tag', nor by deadline, cannot change font size, no time stamp inside to-dos. Plus:
No alphabetical sort of projects in sidebar
No collapsing of areas in "sidebar "
Spotlight integration is gone.
Additionally:
No collapsing of the new headings within projects 
Loss of shading impedes ease of the "form filling " aspect of using the app. Things 2 had a superb UI design, attractive and guiding  the user 's eye. We now have white space 
Loss of colour coding of areas - no green icons, except in Someday 
No location-based to dos 
Still no repeating to dos in projects 
Too much white space on the screen ( see above). It's harsh on the eye and creates glare.
Things 3 "What's new" says " When you open a to-do, it smoothly transforms into a clear white piece of paper, ready for your thoughts. " A blank canvas may be helpful if I'm writing a book or a journal, but Things is essentially a database and I find the structure of a form helpful when entering data.
Notes still cannot be hidden
No undo or cancel button e.g. Creating a new to do
I have difficulty in moving around the app - I'm not finding it intuitive 
You can't switch to landscape view  (being locked in portrait feels claustrophobic to me)
The new 'headings' feature looks quite useful, but what is its intended purpose? If it's really defining a sub-task, why can't you mark it 'done'?
The checklist feature is rather in the same category. Nifty, but isn't it really a sub-task? I can't figure out how to archive a checklist for future use, a feature that would be very handy and would justify the use of the term 'checklist'.
The very useful improvements and new features of Things 3 have probably all been covered in the avalanche of positive reviews, so I won't mention them here. It is a good app in many ways , but a long way (in my view) from being brilliant . It is a surprise to me that I much prefer Things 2! Having said that, my 2 star marking is tongue-in-cheek - or just plain cheek! - the app is much better than that. But when you're the devil's advocate, needs must😊. I hope the developer will enhance and improve the features of Things 3, to build on the excellent work they have already done.

I was a long time user of Things from the start but moved to Trello during the long wait for v3. 
I like that it's familiar and less complicated. So my guess at this stage is that it will become my No1 task organiser again. I'll update this once I have put Things 3 through its paces. Only then might it earn the 5th star. (Hint to CC - don't nag for reviews too early - I can't tell how good it is until I have I've had chance to fully test it out for a few weeks)

I have some feature requests.

I would like to be able to:

1. Collapse project notes (I have about a screen and a half of notes).

2. Attach documents to tasks (or integrate with iCloud Drive so I can link to files).

3. Collapse Areas.

4. Freely rename Upcoming, Anytime, and Someday.

5. Add another group between Anytime and Upcoming called Next, so I can prioritise things in Anytime to schedule and prioritise next.

6. Change the icons (or the colours) of Areas to make them visually easier to spot. 

7. Have a Tags area in the sidebar and the ability to show some tasks grouped by tag (e.g. Important) across all Projects and Areas. 

Additionally, the stats feature in Todoist is really cool 😉😉
